AI.motivation: Detecting ambivalence and hesitancy in unconstrained video is challenging due to the subtle and ambiguous nature of the target signal.
AI.method: CF-Net uses a multimodal approach, encoding visual, audio, and transcript streams with frozen backbones, and fuses them via a ConflictFusion module to compute cross-modal incongruence.
AI.result: CF-Net achieves a Macro F1 of 0.7155 on the BAH validation set and 0.7364 (AP = 0.7492) on the private challenge test set.
AI.conclusion: The proposed CF-Net demonstrates effective performance in detecting ambivalence and hesitancy in unconstrained video, leveraging multimodal fusion and conflict computation.

title: Screening Is Effective for Visual Recognition
summary: Vision Transformer (ViT) has been widely used as a powerful framework for modeling global dependencies among image patches. However, its core component, self-attention assigns softmax-normalized relative weights to all patches, making it difficult to evaluate the relevance between patches independently. In visual recognition, images often contain many background or redundant patches, yet self-attention cannot explicitly reject such irrelevant patches, which may introduce unnecessary information into feature aggregation. To address this limitation, Screening has been proposed in the field of language modeling, where the relevance of each token is independently evaluated based on query-key similarity and low-relevance tokens are explicitly excluded through thresholding. In this work, we propose VisionScreen, a new vision model that extends Screening mechanism to visual recognition. VisionScreen treats image patches as tokens arranged on a two-dimensional grid and extends absolute relevance estimation based on query-key similarity to the two-dimensional spatial domain. This allows each patch to selectively aggregate only content-wise and spatially relevant patches without relying on competition among patches. Experiments on image classification benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional ViT. These results suggest that Screening can be effective for visual recognition, offering an alternative to relative feature aggregation based on softmax attention.

AI.tldr: A new vision model called VisionScreen is proposed, extending the Screening mechanism from language modeling to visual recognition, allowing for selective aggregation of relevant patches.
AI.motivation: The self-attention mechanism in Vision Transformers (ViT) has limitations in evaluating patch relevance independently, leading to unnecessary information in feature aggregation, especially with background or redundant patches.
AI.method: VisionScreen extends the Screening mechanism to the two-dimensional spatial domain, treating image patches as tokens on a grid, and selectively aggregates content-wise and spatially relevant patches.
AI.result: Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that VisionScreen outperforms conventional ViT, suggesting the effectiveness of Screening in visual recognition.
AI.conclusion: The proposed VisionScreen offers an alternative to relative feature aggregation based on softmax attention, demonstrating the potential of Screening in visual recognition tasks.

title: Task-Specific Feature Fusion Method for Multi-Task Affective Behavior Analysis
comment: Extended arXiv version with an appendix. Code will be made publicly available
summary: The 11th Affective Behavior Analysis in-the-wild (ABAW11) Multi-Task Learning Challenge requires a unified system to predict valence-arousal, categorical expressions, and facial action units from the official s-Aff-Wild2 images. Although these tasks are naturally related through facial behavior, our validation experiments show that they benefit from different visual features, temporal processing strategies, fusion mechanisms, and calibration procedures. In this paper, we study task-adaptive feature fusion for ABAW11 multi-task affective behavior analysis. We first adapt two pretrained visual backbones, DINOv2 ViT-L and DINOv3 ConvNeXt-base, on an external expression-oriented facial image set and then freeze them to extract complementary frame-level features from the official ABAW11 data. On top of these frozen features, we systematically compare frame-level prediction heads, temporal convolutional heads, post-hoc temporal smoothing, LightGBM models, feature concatenation, gated fusion, residual fusion, late logit fusion, threshold calibration, and shared MTL structures. The final system selects task-specific fusion and prediction strategies rather than forcing all tasks to share a single architecture. On the ABAW11 validation set, the selected system achieves an EXPR macro-F1 of 0.4222, an AU macro-F1 of 0.5402, and a mean VA CCC of 0.6717, resulting in an overall validation score of 1.6341. The results suggest that task-adaptive fusion of frozen visual features is a simple and effective strategy for ABAW-style multi-task affective behavior analysis.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a task-adaptive feature fusion approach for multi-task affective behavior analysis in the ABAW11 challenge, achieving better results by selecting task-specific fusion and prediction strategies.
AI.motivation: The ABAW11 challenge requires a unified system to predict valence-arousal, categorical expressions, and facial action units, but these tasks benefit from different visual features and processing strategies.
AI.method: The paper adapts pretrained visual backbones (DINOv2 ViT-L and DINOv3 ConvNeXt-base) on an external facial image set, freezes them to extract frame-level features, and systematically compares various prediction heads, fusion mechanisms, and calibration procedures.
AI.result: The selected system achieves an EXPR macro-F1 of 0.4222, an AU macro-F1 of 0.5402, and a mean VA CCC of 0.6717, resulting in an overall validation score of 1.6341 on the ABAW11 validation set.
AI.conclusion: The results suggest that task-adaptive fusion of frozen visual features is a simple and effective strategy for ABAW-style multi-task affective behavior analysis.

title: M$^\text{4}$World: A Multi-view Multimodal Driving World Model for Interactive Object Manipulation and Minute-long Streaming
summary: Driving-world generation has emerged as a core capability for scalable autonomous-driving simulation, yet existing methods remain limited in object-level controllability and long-horizon stability. We present M$^\text{4}$World, a Multi-view and Multimodal generative driving world model that synthesizes future surround-view video streams and synchronized LiDAR scans while supporting interactive object Manipulation and stable Minute-long streaming. Fine-grained object manipulation is realized through a flexible conditioning interface that supports explicit control over both the spatial layout and visual appearance of individual objects. Stable minute-long streaming, on the other hand, is achieved through a multi-stage training framework that enables online causal generation in only four denoising steps while maintaining coherent world dynamics throughout extended rollouts. Building on these components, we introduce an efficient few-clip post-training as well as a suite of visual reference-conditioned generation models, preserving general generation ability while allowing rare-case customization for long-tail controllability. To assess controllability beyond realism, we further introduce an automated VLM-based judging pipeline that evaluates scene-level condition adherence, view-wise object controllability, and cross-view object consistency. Comprehensive experiments show that M$^\text{4}$World consistently delivers high generation quality, precise controllability, and stable minute-long streaming. Together with downstream long-tail augmentation and scene editing, these results demonstrate the potential of M$^\text{4}$World for controllable, scalable driving simulation.

AI.tldr: M^4World is a generative model for autonomous driving simulation that synthesizes surround-view video streams and LiDAR scans with interactive object manipulation and stable long-term streaming.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for driving-world generation are limited in object-level controllability and long-horizon stability, which are crucial for scalable autonomous-driving simulation.
AI.method: M^4World uses a multi-view and multimodal generative approach with a flexible conditioning interface for object manipulation and a multi-stage training framework for stable long-term streaming.
AI.result: M^4World demonstrates high generation quality, precise controllability, and stable minute-long streaming, with potential for controllable and scalable driving simulation.
AI.conclusion: M^4World shows promising results for autonomous driving simulation, enabling interactive object manipulation and stable long-term streaming, with applications in long-tail augmentation and scene editing.

title: From Pixels to States: Rethinking Interactive World Models as Game Engines
summary: Building interactive worlds that respond coherently to player actions has long been a shared goal of computer graphics, games, and artificial intelligence. Recent video generative models provide a data-driven route toward this goal by predicting future observations conditioned on user actions, and are increasingly regarded as potential next-generation game engines. Realizing a genuinely interactive game world, however, requires interaction outcomes that follow rules over evolving game conditions, consequences that persist over long horizons, and a generation loop that operates in real time. Conventional game engines realize these properties through a recurrent action-state-observation loop, in which player actions update an explicit game state according to predefined rules and observations are rendered from the resulting state. Taking this loop as an organizing lens, this paper examines interactive game world modeling along four dimensions: player action control, game state dynamics, state-observation persistence, and real-time interactive generation. For each dimension, we start from the capabilities required by an interactive game world, group existing approaches into representative families, and discuss the strengths and trade-offs of each family. Complementing this analysis, we present a scalable data engine for Black Myth: Wukong that collects over 90 hours of gameplay with frame-aligned player actions, ground-truth game states, and visual observations, together with structured and semantic annotations, as a resource for state-aware game world modeling. We hope this paper offers a clear picture of where the field stands and fosters progress toward interactive game worlds.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes interactive game world modeling through four dimensions and presents a data engine for creating a scalable game world.
AI.motivation: To build interactive worlds that respond coherently to player actions, which is a shared goal of computer graphics, games, and artificial intelligence.
AI.method: The paper examines interactive game world modeling along four dimensions: player action control, game state dynamics, state-observation persistence, and real-time interactive generation.
AI.result: The paper provides an analysis of existing approaches to interactive game world modeling, grouped into representative families, and discusses their strengths and trade-offs. Additionally, a scalable data engine for Black Myth: Wukong is presented.
AI.conclusion: The paper aims to provide a clear picture of the current state of the field and foster progress toward interactive game worlds.

title: VideoRAE: Taming Video Foundation Models for Generative Modeling via Representation Autoencoders
summary: Video generative models commonly rely on latent spaces learned by 3D Variational Autoencoders (3D-VAEs). However, conventional 3D-VAEs are mainly optimized for pixel-level reconstruction, which can limit the semantic and spatio-temporal structure captured by their latents. Meanwhile, Video Foundation Models (VFMs) such as V-JEPA 2 and VideoMAEv2 show strong video understanding capabilities, yet whether their frozen representations can be transformed into compact, reconstruction-capable, and generation-friendly video latents remains largely unexplored. We answer this question with VideoRAE, a representation autoencoder that leverages multi-scale hierarchical features from a frozen video foundation encoder and compresses them with a lightweight 1D self-attention projector. VideoRAE supports both continuous latents for Diffusion Transformers and discrete tokens for autoregressive models via multi-codebook high-dimensional quantization. During decoding, a local-and-global representation alignment objective with the frozen VFM teacher improves semantic preservation and enables training without KL regularization. Experiments show that VideoRAE achieves strong reconstruction in both continuous and discrete regimes. On UCF-101, it obtains state-of-the-art class-to-video gFVDs of 40 and 93 with AR and DiT generators, respectively, while converging approximately 5x faster than competing autoencoder baselines. In a controlled 2B-scale text-to-video study, replacing LTX-VAE with VideoRAE leads to faster convergence under comparable settings. These results validate frozen VFM representations as versatile and generation-friendly video latents. The model and code will be released on https://zhxie0117.github.io/VideoRAE.

AI.tldr: VideoRAE, a representation autoencoder, leverages frozen video foundation model (VFM) features to create compact, generation-friendly video latents, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction and generation results.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D Variational Autoencoders (3D-VAEs) are limited in capturing semantic and spatio-temporal structures, while Video Foundation Models (VFMs) have shown strong video understanding capabilities but their representations need to be transformed into compact and generation-friendly video latents.
AI.method: VideoRAE uses a lightweight 1D self-attention projector to compress multi-scale hierarchical features from a frozen VFM encoder, supporting both continuous and discrete latents for diffusion transformers and autoregressive models.
AI.result: VideoRAE achieves state-of-the-art class-to-video gFVDs of 40 and 93 with AR and DiT generators on UCF-101, converging approximately 5x faster than competing autoencoder baselines, and shows faster convergence in a controlled 2B-scale text-to-video study.
AI.conclusion: The proposed VideoRAE validates frozen VFM representations as versatile and generation-friendly video latents, enabling strong reconstruction and generation results in both continuous and discrete regimes.
